newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stock market hounded by property fears.
newsitem.headline: Manila stock market hounded by property fears.

text.p: Concerns over a glut in the Philippine property market won't be easily dispelled and are likely to continue to cast a pall over the local stock market, analysts said on Friday.
"To most foreign fund managers, this property glut is an issue and investors would rather play it safe and stay out of the sector," said Pamela Pena, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.

"People will be cautious and defensive on property issues for the rest of the year. The negative sentiment surrounding the property sector may still yank blue chip Ayala Land to even cheaper levels," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc.

BPI Securities Corp analyst Bernadette Tamayo said concerns of a glut in the local property sector started last year and were aggravated by the negative effect on Thai stocks of a slump in Thailand's real estate market.

Anscor Hagedorn Securities said the country's biggest property firm, Ayala Land Inc, had seen a 72 percent drop in land sales in the first quarter of this year and a 52 percent decline in middle-income housing sales.
Nervous investors on Friday gave a fresh battering to property shares, with share prices of two leading companies dropping to their lowest levels of the year.
Despite troubles for property stocks, Manila shares on Friday ended 17.11 points higher, or 0.58 percent, at 2,944.98.

"We see a lot of comparisons with Thailand and the exposure of banks that have the biggest market capitalisation here had affected the stock market negatively," said Cilette Liboro, vice-president for research at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
The loan portfolios of local banks are estimated to have about 10 to 11 percent exposure to property companies.
The recent debt problems of Victorias Milling Co, though the result of different factors, have only underlined the issue of problem loans, analysts said.
Cash-depleted sugar miller Victorias was forced last month to seek a 90-day moratorium from 32 creditors on principal repayments on its mounting debts.
Rising interest rates in the U.S. have also led to a sell-off in the sector.

Recent rumours that companies Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and its unit Empire East Land Holdings Inc were cash-strapped also dampened sentiment towards the sector despite repeated denials by the companies.
Megaworld closed at 5.30 pesos and Empire East Land at 5.20, both lows for the year.
"Even Ayala Land, which is the McDonald's of the property sector, has acknowledged that it needs to rework some of its projects," Reyes said.
Ayala Land president Francisco Licuanan earlier said that an oversupply in luxury apartments may come about in 1999. Ayala said it will put emphasis on the burgeoning middle-income housing market.
Joey Salceda, director at SBC Warburg said: "Aggressive underweighting of the properties and the banks remain the central theme to foreign investors.
